cues.en: All right.
In this lecture, we are going to look at why Dijkstra's algorithm does not work with negative cycle.
Now before continuing, let's first identify what a negative cycle means in a graph.
So let's say we have a graph like this.
So the cycle means that if you start from any given vertex and going through other vertices you can
come to this vertex.
It means that we have a cycle in this graph.
So let's say we start from a we can go to the d, then we can go to B.
Then we can go from B to A.
And we can easily see that we started from A.
And we can easily come to the A through other vertices.
And this is a cycle in the graph.
Now negative cycle means that if the sum of the weights of these edges are less than zero, in this
case it means that we have a negative cycle.
So in our case from A to D it is negative six.
Then from d to B it is one and from b to a it is three.
And if you sum up them it's going to be negative two.
So this means that in this graph we have a negative cycle.
So the issue with the negative cycle is that we can never find the minimum distance in a negative cycle.
So if you try to find a path from A to B we need to go to the D.
Then from D we need to go to B.
Then here we have successfully reached the B.
So as you can see the weight is negative five because from A to D be.
It's negative six and from D to be it is one.
So if you sum up them it's going to be negative five.
Now if we do one cycle over here.
So let's say we go from B to A and come back from A to D then B again the distance is going to change.
So as you can see until b the distance was negative five.
So from a to b it is three.
Then from A to d it is negative six.
And from d to b it is one.
So if you sum up them is going to be negative seven.
So as you can see the distance decrease.
And in case of Dijkstra's algorithm we are looking for the shortest distance.
So as you can see in this case it is decrease.
Now if I do one more cycle over here at every cycle the distance decreases.
So this will continue without stopping.
So that's why if you have a negative cycle the Dijkstra's algorithm cannot find the shortest path.
So the question is how to deal with this situation.
So we can return a message to your user saying that there is a negative cycle in the graph.
So Dijkstra's algorithm cannot proceed.
But the problem is Dijkstra's algorithm cannot catch the negative cycle, so we cannot stop it.
So to deal this we have another algorithm which is Bellman-ford algorithm.
Now in case of Bellman-ford algorithm we can catch the negative cycle, but we cannot do anything about
it.
We can just inform the users saying that there is a negative cycle in the graph.
Now in our upcoming sessions, we are going to learn about the Bellman-ford algorithm.
